Introduction to unit crystal lattice and unit cell

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
$$\text{Order parameter }S=\tfrac{1}{2}\left\langle 3\cos^{2}\theta-1\right\rangle\ (S=0\ \text{isotropic},\ S=1\ \text{perfect crystal})$$
$$\text{Birefringence: }n_{\parallel}\neq n_{\perp},\qquad \varepsilon_{\parallel}\neq\varepsilon_{\perp}$$
$$\text{Cholesteric reflection: }\lambda_{\max}=n\,p\ (p=\text{helical pitch, temperature dependent})$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Liquid crystals are crystals that have partly melted. ✅ They form a distinct mesophase: molecules flow yet keep orientational order.  ·  ❌ Liquid crystals emit light. ✅ LCDs modulate transmitted light from a backlight — they are non-emissive.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Cholesteryl benzoate (Reinitzer, 1888) was the first liquid crystal studied.  ·  Display nematic LCs are usually cyanobiphenyl homologues with a mesophase range of only a few tens of degrees.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Why does an LCD watch darken in a very hot car? **Solution:** heating pushes the material above its mesophase range, the ordered phase is lost, polarisation can no longer be controlled and the display becomes unreadable.  ·  **Problem:** A thermochromic LC strip shows red at 30 °C and blue at 35 °C. Why? **Solution:** the helical pitch shortens with rising temperature, so the reflected (Bragg) wavelength moves from red towards blue — a visual thermometer.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: liquid crystals, their applications (within States of Matter).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning  ·  Liquid crystals are substances that are simultaneously partly ordered like a crystal and partly mobile like a liquid — a mesophase intermediate between the crystalline solid and the isotropic liquid. They flow and take the shape of the container, yet their rod- or disc-shaped molecules retain positional/orientational order, so their optical, electrical and mechanical properties are **anisotropic**…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Kevlar, a liquid-crystal polymer, has a strength-to-weight ratio several times that of steel.  ·  answer pattern for "Liquid crystals and their applications": define → method → result. Structure earns the marks on 6–10 mark questions.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. Characteristics  ·  • Molecules are elongated (rod-like) or flat and disc-like with flexible end chains; shape anisotropy produces the ordered mesophase.  ·  • Partial order gives birefringence (two refractive indices), anisotropic dielectric constant, viscosity, elasticity and magnetic susceptibility.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ They are liquids containing suspended crystal particles. ✅ The order is molecular and inherent to the phase.  ·  ❌ Liquid crystal displays work by melting. ✅ They work by electric-field reorientation of molecules within the same mesophase.  ·  ❌ A liquid crystal thermometer measures heat capacity. ✅ It uses the temperature dependence of the helical pitch, which shifts the reflected colour.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Quote the narrow temperature window as the main practical limitation.  ·  Distinguish thermotropic from lyotropic liquid crystals and describe nematic, smectic and cholesteric mesophases.  ·  Explain the working of a twisted-nematic liquid crystal display.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: List four applications of liquid crystals in everyday life and industry.  ·  Explain how liquid crystals measure temperature and map thermal hot spots.  ·  State the limitations of liquid-crystal materials in devices.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • Order-disorder change occurs over a narrow, well-defined **temperature range** — below it a solid, above it an ordinary liquid.  ·  • **Thermotropic** LCs form on temperature change (displays); **lyotropic** LCs form in solution when concentration changes (soap, detergents, cell membranes).  ·  ### 3. Classified mesophases
